freeze_policy: v11 builds no packet from live product sources and takes no new prompt-size measurement. Its archive binds this protocol, the v10 supersession record, the inherited v10 archive state and artifacts by digest, and the carried r1 evidence. Its freeze additionally binds the digests of the v11 runner, the v11 evidence validator, scripts/evals/run-reviewer-holdout.py, scripts/ci/lib/strict_json.py, scripts/ci/lib/version_contract.py (imported by strict_json.py), and scripts/evals/eval_security.py, and none of them may change until the schedule is terminal. The canonical freeze must record those four shared tools at a25fa410, 5fbff804, 68039f66, and c0f760ac respectively; the runner and validator digests are bound by the freeze itself. Before reserving a fresh attempt, the runner validates the archive state, compares the live pre-call integrity snapshot with the freeze-derived expectation, checks that the start time is not earlier than the predecessor's finish time, and refuses report path fields or a temporary directory that would still record an account home path after normalization; any mismatch aborts without consuming the attempt. Drift observed after reservation makes that attempt INCONCLUSIVE.

local_runner.provenance_boundary: Exact local native CLI hash/version; absolute path is recorded only as local run provenance, with caller-declared model/provider provenance and no remote model attestation.
local_runner.timeout_disclosure: Fixed at 1800 seconds for both fresh attempts. Any other --timeout value is rejected before reservation, and the value is recorded in the reservation and the report. v10 bound no timeout: r1's value was not recorded (runner default 900 seconds) and r1 took 592,668 ms. This is a harness-only change that does not alter the prompt, model, or scoring.

vendor_manifest.recovery: If the local build is unavailable, re-fetch version 2.1.220 for this platform from the vendor release channel and accept it only if its SHA-256 equals checksum_sha256 and its size equals size.

model_catalog.provenance_boundary: Local model identity only. Each slug is recorded because it occurs verbatim in the pinned local Claude Code executable at the pinned SHA-256, which is a local provenance fact, not a vendor catalog. No local source establishes a context window, maximum output, or price for these models, so this phase declares none and asserts no context-window, effective-context, or output-reserve budget. This is not remote model attestation.

report_normalization.rule: Replace the operator account's home-directory prefix with the placeholder home /Users/user/; no other byte changes.

carried_attempts.validation: Validated with the inherited v10 attempt checks against the inherited v10 protocol, packet, manifest, prompt-size attestation, source snapshot, remediation ledger, model catalog, freeze, and v10 schedule digest, including exact reference-tokenizer replay and independent recomputation of review, decision, and status from the raw bytes, with exactly one correction: the expected integrity_before and integrity_after also contain corrected_integrity_key. Reservation and raw bytes must hash to the digests above, and the report must hash to report_sha256.

claim_boundary: v11 was designed after observing v10 r1's valid FAIL: overall_score 88.67 < 90, C0/H0/M8, reopened_target_ids [V8-T4], with failed checks overall_score and selected_remediations_not_reopened.

V8-T4 was reopened mechanically by the category/file/severity rule, through a false_positive_control Medium finding at skills/e2e-reviewer/scripts/scan.sh:756 ('Lexer helper discards awk failures, silently narrowing framework scope'), not by a recurrence of the historical 'Cypress basename bypasses foreign-framework exclusion' defect. The matcher is left unchanged.
v11 changes only harness code. Rubric, thresholds, ledger targets, packet, prompt bytes, model catalog, CLI pin, host matrix, and model order are inherited from v10 by SHA-256.

r1 is counted under a validator that differs from the frozen v10 validator c94b0c66 by accepting superseded_phase_record_sha256 in integrity_before and integrity_after, the key the frozen runner b838f6de always emits. Every other v10 check is unchanged. The frozen validator still rejects r1.
The v11 aggregate is predetermined FAIL under the FAIL-first rule. r2 and r3 are completion and descriptive observations, and no v11 result can overturn, replace, or erase r1.

Release commit 474b3d1 froze protocol 8f4bb107 on packet 35bb3b26 (source snapshot 8649cafb, a 440,800-byte prompt, 119,584 reference tokens), and that freeze shipped in the 1.11.0 release commit and in tags v1.12.0 through v1.15.1. That replacement was not recorded in the 679f2c4 commit message, CHANGELOG, or STATUS text. The carried r1 report is account-normalized (5 path fields; original sha f1fe1d71, carried sha 1098e8c3). Reservation and raw bytes are unchanged, and review, decision, and status are identical.

The reviewed object is source snapshot d01dc69d, a combination of seven files that never shipped together in any release (v1.16.0-era SKILL.md files with scan.sh 6e6df9a9). It is not v1.16.3, and no claim covers the installed release or any surface outside those seven.

Model coverage is claude-opus-5 twice and claude-fable-5 once within one provider family: unbalanced, not cross-provider, and no per-model rate.

The exact CLI pin (2.1.220) is kept instead of AGENTS.md's 'minimum' guidance, which applies to reviewer-holdout execution_identity, because the carried r1 and the fresh attempts must share one CLI identity and the claude-opus-5 prompt-length acceptance was measured on that build.
Local runner and model strings are provenance, not remote model attestation. The o200k_base count is a size proxy, not Anthropic tokenization.

The inherited v10 remediation ledger 0896a55a is used unchanged, so its own superseded_phase still names v9 and its target dispositions still read pending_canonical_v10_freeze. v11 binds the v10 supersession through phase_binding.superseded_phase instead of cutting a new ledger.

The inherited aggregate_rule passage says a target is reopened in 'the same category and exact affected file set'. The inherited matcher, unchanged in v11, reopens a target when a finding has the target's category, cites one file that is a member of the target's affected_files, and has a severity at or above the historical severity. The wording matters for PV8-C2 and PV8-C3, whose affected_files hold two paths, and not for V8-T4. The passage is read as that membership rule.

A fresh attempt's finished_at_utc is the later of the wall clock at finish and started_at_utc plus the monotonic elapsed time, and a recovery report's is the later of the wall clock and the reserved start, so a backward wall-clock step cannot record a finish before its start. A next attempt whose wall-clock start precedes that finish is refused before reservation.

The canonical v10 archive stays FROZEN with no attempts and remains valid under its frozen validator. r1's bytes are carried only into the v11 archive. This phase does not change v8, the v9 record, or v10, and it is not unbiased defect discovery, remediation confirmation, cross-provider evidence, full product coverage, skill accuracy, human or sealed review, independent ground truth, or remote model attestation.

inherited_frozen_phase.inheritance_rule: The rubric, output contract, and packet contract (caps, surface scope, prompt rendering, and reference tokenizer) are read from the inherited v10 protocol bytes at protocol_path, which must hash to protocol_sha256; they are not duplicated here. The packet, packet manifest, prompt-size attestation, and source snapshot are read from the inherited archive by digest and cross-checked against each other. No v11 packet is built from live product sources and no new prompt-size measurement is taken: the inherited attestation is replayed exactly.

purpose: Complete the preregistered v10 Claude-only remediation-confirmation schedule after its measured harness defect. The consumed v10 attempt claude-v8-remediation-confirmation-v10-r1, a valid FAIL, is carried as schedule index 0, and only the two never-reserved schedule slots run as fresh v11 attempts on the byte-identical inherited v10 packet, prompt, rubric, remediation ledger, model catalog, host matrix, and pinned CLI. Only harness bytes change: the v11 runner, evidence validator, unit suite, and evidence wrapper, plus the shared zero-tool runner revision disclosed in phase_binding.claim_boundary. Under the FAIL-first rule a completed aggregate can only be FAIL, so the fresh attempts are completion and descriptive observations. This post-hoc protocol is preregistered after observing r1 and before any v11 model call. It is not unbiased defect discovery, remediation confirmation, cross-provider evidence, full product coverage, skill accuracy, human or sealed review, independent ground truth, or remote model attestation.

aggregate_rule.completion: Every scheduled attempt ID must appear exactly once in schedule order. Schedule index 0 is the carried v10 attempt claude-v8-remediation-confirmation-v10-r1: it is never re-run, and it counts only when its reservation, raw, and normalized report bytes hash to the digests bound in carried_from and its content validates against the inherited v10 protocol, packet, source snapshot, remediation ledger, model catalog, freeze, and v10 schedule digest with the one corrected integrity key declared in phase_binding.carried_attempts. Indexes 1 and 2 are fresh v11 attempts that share the one inherited packet, inherited protocol, source snapshot, inherited remediation ledger, and this schedule digest. Historical, replacement, retry, or ad-hoc attempts do not count, and the never-reserved v10 attempt IDs claude-v8-remediation-confirmation-v10-r2 and claude-v8-remediation-confirmation-v10-r3 can never count. Every present reservation and terminal report, the carried one included, must bind one globally unique UUIDv4 invocation_id; duplicates make partial or complete evidence invalid. invocation_id values must round-trip as lowercase canonical RFC 4122 UUIDv4 values. Each attempt must finish at or after it starts, and each later attempt must start at or after its predecessor finishes, so index 1 cannot start before the carried attempt's finish time 2026-09-17T01:50:46.467Z.
aggregate_rule.passage: All three attempts must have an individual PASS verdict, and no finding may reopen any of the nine bound targets at or above its historical severity in the same category and exact affected file set. Aggregate evaluation is FAIL-first: any valid FAIL makes a completed aggregate FAIL even if another attempt is INCONCLUSIVE. The carried index-0 attempt is already a valid FAIL (overall_score 88.67, V8-T4 reopened), so a completed v11 aggregate can only be FAIL; the two fresh attempts are completion and descriptive observations and cannot change that gate. Model coverage is claude-opus-5 twice and claude-fable-5 once, so the schedule is deliberately unbalanced and supports no per-model rate; both models share one provider family, so a completed aggregate is cross-model within Anthropic and is never cross-provider evidence.

status_policy.FAIL: The strict payload and provenance are intact, but a threshold fails or one of the nine bound targets is reopened. Aggregate evaluation is FAIL-first.
status_policy.INCONCLUSIVE: The call, strict payload, canonical evidence, reference-tokenizer prompt-size replay, predecessor binding, superseded-phase binding, inherited-phase binding, carried-attempt binding, or causal producer evidence is missing or invalid. A prompt that a model rejects for length, or a call that exceeds local_runner.timeout_seconds, also lands here, because this phase declares no context-window fit. A consumed RESERVED or RAW attempt may be terminalized without another model call: pre-raw recovery commits a terminal_error raw, while post-raw recovery preserves and hashes the existing canonical raw, even when it is empty.
status_policy.PASS: The strict payload and all evidence are complete, every fixed threshold passes, and none of the nine bound targets is reopened.
status_policy.fail_first_determination: The carried index-0 attempt is a valid FAIL, so under the FAIL-first rule a completed v11 aggregate can only be FAIL and no aggregate PASS exists for this phase. An incomplete archive still has no aggregate gate, and neither fresh attempt can change the completed gate.
